verses.zh: 先知以利沙叫了一个先知门徒来，吩咐他说：「你束上腰，手拿这瓶膏油往基列的拉末去。
verses.en: Now Elisha the prophet summoned a member of the prophetic guild[NOTE:1] and told him, “Tuck your robes into your belt, take this container[NOTE:2] of olive oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
notes: Heb “one of the sons of the prophets.”
Or “flask.”

verses.zh: 到了那里，要寻找宁示的孙子、约沙法的儿子耶户，使他从同僚中起来，带他进严密的屋子，
verses.en: When you arrive there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi and take him aside into an inner room.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and go and set him apart from his brothers and bring him into an inner room in an inner room.”

verses.zh: 将瓶里的膏油倒在他头上，说：『耶和华如此说：我膏你作以色列王。』说完了，就开门逃跑，不要迟延。」
verses.en: Take the container of olive oil, pour it over his head, and say, ‘This is what the Lord has said, “I have designated[NOTE:1] you as king over Israel.”’ Then open the door and run away quickly!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “anointed.”
Heb “and open the door and run away and do not delay.”

verses.zh: 于是那少年先知往基列的拉末去了。
verses.en: So the young prophet[NOTE:1] went to Ramoth Gilead.
notes: Heb “the young man, the young man, the prophet.” The MT is probably dittographic, the phrase “the young man” being accidentally repeated. The phrases “the young man” and “the prophet” are appositional, with the latter qualifying more specifically the former.

verses.zh: 到了那里，看见众军长都坐着，就说：「将军哪，我有话对你说。」耶户说：「我们众人里，你要对哪一个说呢？」回答说：「将军哪，我要对你说。」
verses.en: When he arrived, the officers of the army were sitting there.[NOTE:1] So he said, “I have a message for you, O officer.”[NOTE:2] Jehu asked, “For which one of us?”[NOTE:3] He replied, “For you, O officer.”
notes: Heb “and he arrived and look, the officers of the army were sitting.”
Heb “[there is] a word for me to you, O officer.”
Heb “To whom from all of us?”

verses.zh: 耶户就起来，进了屋子，少年人将膏油倒在他头上，对他说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『我膏你作耶和华民以色列的王。
verses.en: So Jehu[NOTE:1] got up and went inside. Then the prophet[NOTE:2] poured the olive oil on his head and said to him, “This is what the Lord God of Israel has said, ‘I have designated you as king over the Lord’s people Israel.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (the prophet) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 你要击杀你主人亚哈的全家，我好在耶洗别身上伸我仆人众先知和耶和华一切仆人流血的冤。
verses.en: You will destroy the family of your master Ahab.[NOTE:1] I will get revenge against Jezebel for the shed blood of my servants the prophets and for the shed blood of all the Lord’s servants.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “strike down the house of Ahab your master.”
Heb “I will avenge the shed blood of my servants the prophets and the shed blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezebel.”

verses.zh: 亚哈全家必都灭亡，凡属亚哈的男丁，无论是困住的、自由的，我必从以色列中剪除，
verses.en: Ahab’s entire family will die. I[NOTE:1] will cut off every last male belonging to Ahab in Israel, including even the weak and incapacitated.[NOTE:2]
notes: The LXX has the second person, “you.”

Heb “and I will cut off from Ahab those who urinate against a wall, [including both those who are] restrained and let free [or, ‘abandoned’] in Israel.” On the phrase וְעָצוּר וְעָזוּב (veʿatsur veʿazur, translated here “weak and incapacitated”) see the note at 1 Kgs 14:10.

verses.zh: 使亚哈的家像尼八儿子耶罗波安的家，又像亚希雅儿子巴沙的家。
verses.en: I will make Ahab’s dynasty[NOTE:1] like those of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.
notes: Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 耶洗别必在耶斯列田里被狗所吃，无人葬埋。』」说完了，少年人就开门逃跑了。
verses.en: Dogs will devour Jezebel on the plot of ground in Jezreel; she will not be buried.’”[NOTE:1] Then he opened the door and ran away.
notes: Note how the young prophet greatly expands the message Elisha had given to him. In addition to lengthening the introductory formula (by adding “the God of Israel”) and the official declaration that accompanies the act of anointing (by adding “the Lord’s people”), he goes on to tell how Jehu will become king (by a revolt against Ahab’s dynasty), makes it clear that Jehu will be an instrument of divine vengeance, and predicts the utter annihilation of Ahab’s family and the violent death of Jezebel.

verses.zh: 耶户出来，回到他主人的臣仆那里，有一人问他说：「平安吗？这狂妄的人来见你有甚么事呢？」回答说：「你们认得那人，也知道他说甚么。」
verses.en: When Jehu rejoined[NOTE:1] his master’s servants, they[NOTE:2] asked him, “Is everything all right?[NOTE:3] Why did this madman visit you?” He replied, “Ah, it’s not important. You know what kind of man he is and the kinds of things he says.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “went out to.”
The MT has the singular, “he said,” but many witnesses correctly read the plural.
Heb “Is there peace?”

Heb “He said, ‘You, you know the man and his thoughts.’” Jehu tries to deflect their question by reminding them that the man is an eccentric individual who says strange things. His reply suggests that the man said nothing of importance. The translation seeks to bring out the tone and intent of Jehu’s reply.

verses.zh: 他们说：「这是假话，你据实地告诉我们。」回答说：「他如此如此对我说。他说：『耶和华如此说：我膏你作以色列王。』」
verses.en: But they said, “You’re lying! Tell us what he said.” So he told them what he had said. He also related how he had said,[NOTE:1] “This is what the Lord has said, ‘I have designated you as king over Israel.’”
notes: Heb “So he said, ‘Like this and like this he said to me, saying.’” The words “like this and like this” are probably not a direct quote of Jehu’s words to his colleagues. Rather this is the narrator’s way of avoiding repetition and indicating that Jehu repeated, or at least summarized, what the prophet had said to him.

verses.zh: 他们就急忙各将自己的衣服铺在上层台阶，使耶户坐在其上；他们吹角，说：「耶户作王了！」
verses.en: Each of them quickly took off his cloak, and they spread them out at Jehu’s[NOTE:1] feet on the steps.[NOTE:2] The trumpet was blown[NOTE:3] and they shouted, “Jehu is[NOTE:4] king!”
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Jehu) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “and they hurried and took, each one his garment, and they placed [them] beneath him on the bone [?] of the steps.” The precise nuance of גֶּרֶם (gerem), “bone,” is unclear. Some suggest the nuance “bare” here; it may be a technical architectural term in this context.
Heb “they blew the trumpet.” This has been translated as a passive to avoid the implication that the same ones who shouted had all blown trumpets.
Or “has become.”

verses.zh: 这样，宁示的孙子、约沙法的儿子耶户背叛约兰。先是约兰和以色列众人因为亚兰王哈薛的缘故，把守基列的拉末；
verses.en: Then Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram.Jehu the AssassinNow Joram had been in Ramoth Gilead with the whole Israelite army,[NOTE:1] guarding against an invasion by King Hazael of Syria.
notes: Heb “he and all Israel.”

verses.zh: 但约兰王回到耶斯列，医治与亚兰王哈薛打仗所受的伤。耶户说：「若合你们的意思，就不容人逃出城往耶斯列报信去。」
verses.en: But King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds he received from the Syrians[NOTE:1] when he fought against King Hazael of Syria.[NOTE:2] Jehu told his supporters,[NOTE:3] “If you really want me to be king,[NOTE:4] then don’t let anyone escape from the city to go and warn Jezreel.”
notes: Heb “which the Syrians inflicted [on] him.”
See 2 Kgs 8:28-29a.
The words “his supporters” are added for clarification.
Heb “If this is your desire.” נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) refers here to the seat of the emotions and will. For other examples of this use of the word, see BDB 660-61 s.v.

verses.zh: 于是耶户坐车往耶斯列去，因为约兰病卧在那里。犹大王亚哈谢已经下去看望他。
verses.en: Jehu drove his chariot[NOTE:1] to Jezreel, for Joram was recuperating[NOTE:2] there. (Now King Ahaziah of Judah had come down to visit[NOTE:3] Joram.)
notes: Heb “rode [or, ‘mounted’] and went.”
Heb “lying down.”
Heb “to see.”

verses.zh: 有一个守望的人站在耶斯列的楼上，看见耶户带着一群人来，就说：「我看见一群人。」约兰说：「打发一个骑马的去迎接他们，问说：平安不平安？」
verses.en: Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel and saw Jehu’s troops approaching.[NOTE:1] He said, “I see troops!”[NOTE:2] Joram[NOTE:3] ordered,[NOTE:4] “Send a rider out to meet them and have him ask, ‘Is everything all right?’”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the quantity [of the men] of Jehu, when he approached.” Elsewhere שִׁפְעַה (shifʿah), “quantity,” is used of a quantity of camels (Isa 60:6) or horses (Ezek 26:10) and of an abundance of water (Job 22:11; 38:34).
The term שִׁפְעַת (shifʿat) appears to be a construct form of the noun, but no genitive follows.
Heb “Jehoram” here and in vv. 21, 22, 23, 24; Joram is a short form of the name Jehoram.
Heb “said.”
Heb “Get a rider and send [him] to meet him and let him ask, ‘Is there peace?’”

verses.zh: 骑马的就去迎接耶户，说：「王问说，平安不平安？」耶户说：「平安不平安与你何干？你转在我后头吧！」守望的人又说：「使者到了他们那里，却不回来。」
verses.en: So the horseman[NOTE:1] went to meet him and said, “This is what the king says, ‘Is everything all right?’”[NOTE:2] Jehu replied, “None of your business![NOTE:3] Follow me.” The watchman reported, “The messenger reached them, but hasn’t started back.”
notes: Heb “the rider of the horse.”
Heb “Is there peace?”
Heb “What concerning you and concerning peace?” That is, “What concern is that to you?”

verses.zh: 王又打发一个骑马的去。这人到了他们那里，说：「王问说，平安不平安？」耶户说：「平安不平安与你何干？你转在我后头吧！」
verses.en: So he sent a second horseman out to them[NOTE:1] and he said, “This is what the king says, ‘Is everything all right?’”[NOTE:2] Jehu replied, “None of your business! Follow me.”
notes: Heb “and he came to them.”
The MT has simply “peace,” omitting the prefixed interrogative particle. It is likely that the particle has been accidentally omitted; several ancient witnesses include it or assume its presence.

verses.zh: 守望的人又说：「他到了他们那里，也不回来；车赶得甚猛，像宁示的孙子耶户的赶法。」
verses.en: The watchman reported, “He reached them, but hasn’t started back. The one who drives the lead chariot drives like Jehu son of Nimshi;[NOTE:1] he drives recklessly.”
notes: Heb “and the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi.”

verses.zh: 约兰吩咐说：「套车！」人就给他套车。以色列王约兰和犹大王亚哈谢各坐自己的车出去迎接耶户，在耶斯列人拿伯的田那里遇见他。
verses.en: Joram ordered, “Hitch up my chariot.”[NOTE:1] When his chariot had been hitched up,[NOTE:2] King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah went out in their respective chariots[NOTE:3] to meet Jehu. They met up with him[NOTE:4] in the plot of land that had once belonged to Naboth of Jezreel.
notes: The words “my chariot” are added for clarification.
Heb “and he hitched up his chariot.”
Heb “each in his chariot and they went out.”
Heb “they found him.”

verses.zh: 约兰见耶户就说：「耶户啊，平安吗？」耶户说：「你母亲耶洗别的淫行邪术这样多，焉能平安呢？」
verses.en: When Joram saw Jehu, he asked, “Is everything all right, Jehu?” He replied, “How can everything be all right as long as your mother Jezebel promotes idolatry and pagan practices?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “How [can there be] peace as long as the adulterous acts of Jezebel your mother and her acts of sorcery [are] many?” In this instance “adulterous acts” is employed metaphorically for idolatry. As elsewhere in the OT, worshiping other gods is viewed as spiritual adultery and unfaithfulness to the one true God. The phrase “many acts of sorcery” could be taken literally, for Jezebel undoubtedly utilized pagan divination practices, but the phrase may be metaphorical, pointing to her devotion to pagan customs in general.

verses.zh: 约兰就转车逃跑，对亚哈谢说：「亚哈谢啊，反了！」
verses.en: Joram turned his chariot around and took off.[NOTE:1] He said to Ahaziah, “It’s a trap,[NOTE:2] Ahaziah!”
notes: Heb “and Jehoram turned his hands and fled.” The phrase “turned his hands” refers to how he would have pulled on the reins in order to make his horses turn around.
Heb “Deceit, Ahaziah.”

verses.zh: 耶户开满了弓，射中约兰的脊背，箭从心窝穿出，约兰就仆倒在车上。
verses.en: Jehu aimed his bow and shot an arrow right between Joram’s shoulders.[NOTE:1] The arrow went through[NOTE:2] his heart and he fell to his knees in his chariot.
notes: Heb “and Jehu filled his hand with the bow and he struck Jehoram between his shoulders.”
Heb “went out from.”

verses.zh: 耶户对他的军长毕甲说：「你把他抛在耶斯列人拿伯的田间。你当追想，你我一同坐车跟随他父亚哈的时候，耶和华对亚哈所说的预言，
verses.en: Jehu ordered[NOTE:1] his officer Bidkar, “Pick him up and throw him into the part of the field that once belonged to Naboth of Jezreel. Remember, you and I were riding together behind his father, Ahab, when the Lord pronounced this oracle against him,
notes: Heb “said to.”

verses.zh: 说：『我昨日看见拿伯的血和他众子的血，我必在这块田上报应你。』这是耶和华说的，现在你要照着耶和华的话，把他抛在这田间。」
verses.en: ‘“Know for sure that I saw the shed blood of Naboth and his sons yesterday,” says the Lord, “and that I will give you what you deserve[NOTE:1] right here in this plot of land,” says the Lord.’ So now pick him up and throw him into this plot of land, just as in the Lord’s message.”
notes: Heb “I will pay you back.”

verses.zh: 犹大王亚哈谢见这光景，就从园亭之路逃跑。耶户追赶他，说：「把这人也杀在车上。」到了靠近以伯莲的姑珥坡上击伤了他。他逃到米吉多，就死在那里。
verses.en: When King Ahaziah of Judah saw what happened, he took off[NOTE:1] up the road to Beth Haggan. Jehu chased him and ordered, “Shoot him too.” They shot him while he was driving his chariot up the ascent of Gur near Ibleam.[NOTE:2] He fled to Megiddo[NOTE:3] and died there.
notes: Heb “and Ahaziah king of Judah saw and fled.”

After Jehu’s order (“kill him too”), the MT has simply, “to the chariot in the ascent of Gur which is near Ibleam.” The main verb in the clause, “they shot him” (וַיַּכֻּהוּ, vayyakkuhu), has been accidentally omitted by virtual haplography/homoioteleuton. Note that the immediately preceding form הַכֻּהוּ (hakkuhu), “shoot him,” ends with the same suffix.
For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

verses.zh: 他的臣仆用车将他的尸首送到耶路撒冷，葬在大卫城他自己的坟墓里，与他列祖同葬。
verses.en: His servants took his body[NOTE:1] back to Jerusalem[NOTE:2] and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.
notes: Heb “drove him.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 亚哈谢登基作犹大王的时候，是在亚哈的儿子约兰第十一年。
verses.en: Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.

verses.zh: 耶户到了耶斯列；耶洗别听见就擦粉、梳头，从窗户里往外观看。
verses.en: Jehu approached Jezreel. When Jezebel heard the news, she put on some eye liner,[NOTE:1] fixed up her hair, and leaned out the window.
notes: Heb “she fixed her eyes with antimony.” Antimony (פּוּךְ, pukh) was used as a cosmetic. The narrator portrays her as a prostitute (see Jer 4:30), a role she has played in the spiritual realm (see the note at v. 22).

verses.zh: 耶户进门的时候，耶洗别说：「杀主人的心利啊，平安吗？」
verses.en: When Jehu came through the gate, she said, “Is everything all right, Zimri, murderer of his master?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Jezebel associates Jehu with another assassin, Zimri, who approximately 44 years before had murdered King Elah, only to meet a violent death just a few days later (1 Kgs 16:9-20). On the surface Jezebel’s actions seem contradictory. On the one hand, she beautifies herself as if to seduce Jehu, but on the other hand, she insults and indirectly threatens him with this comparison to Zimri. Upon further reflection, however, her actions reveal a clear underlying motive. She wants to retain her power, not to mention her life. By beautifying herself, she appeals to Jehu’s sexual impulses; by threatening him, she reminds him that he is in the same precarious position as Zimri. But, if he makes Jezebel his queen, he can consolidate his power. In other words through her actions and words Jezebel is saying to Jehu, “You desire me, don’t you? And you need me!”

verses.zh: 耶户抬头向窗户观看，说：「谁顺从我？」有两三个太监从窗户往外看他。
verses.en: He looked up at the window and said, “Who is on my side? Who?” Two or three[NOTE:1] eunuchs looked down at him.
notes: Heb “two, three.” The narrator may be intentionally vague or uncertain here, or the two numbers may represent alternate traditions.

verses.zh: 耶户说：「把她扔下来！」他们就把她扔下来。她的血溅在墙上和马上；于是把她践踏了。
verses.en: He said, “Throw her down!” So they threw her down, and when she hit the ground,[NOTE:1] her blood splattered against the wall and the horses, and Jehu drove his chariot over her.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “when she hit the ground” are added for stylistic reasons.
Heb “and he trampled her.”

verses.zh: 耶户进去，吃了喝了，吩咐说：「你们把这被咒诅的妇人葬埋了，因为她是王的女儿。」
verses.en: He went inside and had a meal.[NOTE:1] Then he said, “Dispose of this accursed woman’s corpse. Bury her, for after all, she was a king’s daughter.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he went in and ate and drank.”
Heb “Attend to this accursed woman and bury her for she was the daughter of a king.”

verses.zh: 他们就去葬埋她，只寻得她的头骨和脚，并手掌。
verses.en: But when they went to bury her, they found nothing left but[NOTE:1] the skull, feet, and palms of the hands.
notes: Heb “they did not find her, except for.”

verses.zh: 他们回去告诉耶户，耶户说：「这正应验耶和华藉他仆人提斯比人以利亚所说的话，说：『在耶斯列田间，狗必吃耶洗别的肉；
verses.en: So they went back and told him. Then he said, “It is the fulfillment of the Lord’s message[NOTE:1] that he had spoken through his servant, Elijah the Tishbite, ‘In the plot of land at Jezreel, dogs will devour Jezebel’s flesh.
notes: Heb “It is the Lord’s message.”

verses.zh: 耶洗别的尸首必在耶斯列田间如同粪土，甚至人不能说这是耶洗别。』」
verses.en: Jezebel’s corpse will be like manure on the surface of the ground in the plot of land at Jezreel. People will not be able to even recognize her.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “so that they will not say, ‘This is Jezebel.’”
